findings.text: follow-on: map run --clear now deletes the MAPS_TO_IMAS edges through the same binding owner but still differs from map clear, which at imas_codex/cli/map.py:686-700 also deletes the mapping's MappingEvidence nodes and the IMASMapping node; a --clear re-run can therefore retain escalation evidence (MERGE'd per escalation at imas_codex/ids/models.py:737) whose escalation no longer holds. Section 6's done-when concerns bindings only, so this does not block, but the section's 'removes what map clear removes' title overstates what landed.

follow-on: the suite patches workers.clear_mapping_bindings with a spy and workers.GraphClient with a MagicMock, so it asserts the engine calls the imported symbol, not that the delete reaches the graph -- the Cypher in graph_ops.clear_mapping_bindings is verified only by the live run, so a rewrite of the query that kept the call would leave every gate assertion green.

follow-on: the receipt is logged only when removed is nonzero ('if removed:'), so a --clear that deletes no bindings is silent and reads the same as a clear that never ran; logging the count unconditionally would let an operator distinguish a zero delete from a skipped clear.
